articles.headline: Thunder overcome SGA's shooting woes to beat Nuggets 96-84 in home opener
keyFacts: The Oklahoma City Thunder beat the Denver Nuggets 96-84 in their home opener on Thursday.
Jalen Williams scored 21 points and Chet Holmgren added 12 points and 17 rebounds for the Thunder.
Shai-Gilgeous-Alexander scored 17 points on 6-of-19 shooting, ending his streak of scoring at least 20 points at 141 games.
body: OKLAHOMA CITY (AP) — Jalen Williams scored 21 points, Chet Holmgren had 12 points and 17 rebounds, and the Oklahoma City Thunder withstood a poor shooting night from Shai-Gilgeous-Alexander in their home opener to beat the Denver Nuggets 96-84 on Thursday.

Gilgeous-Alexander, who scored 32 points in a convincing win over San Antonio on Tuesday night, finished with 17 points on 6-of-19 shooting against Denver. He failed to score 20 points for the first time in 141 games.

The league's two-time reigning MVP missed all seven shots he took in the first 24 minutes as the Thunder trailed by as many as nine points. A pair of free throws kept him from going scoreless in a half for the first time since his rookie year with the Clippers in 2019.

It marked just the fourth time in 450 games with the Thunder he's gone without a field goal in a half in. Gilgeous-Alexander scored the first basket of the third quarter to pull Oklahoma City to 48-46.
Aaron Gordon scored 20 points and Nikola Jokic and DeMar DeRozan added 13 apiece for Denver, which was playing its first game.

A layup by Mitchell gave the Thunder a 64-62 lead — their first since 3-0 — and 3-pointers by Alex Caruso and Alexander extended it to 70-64 after three quarters. Oklahoma City extended the advantage to 93-76 on a 3 by Gilgeous-Alexander to give him 17 points with 1:44 left. He then asked to be taken out during a timeout and did not return to the game.
Up next
Nuggets: Host New Orleans on Saturday night.
Thunder: Host the Los Angeles Clippers on Sunday night.

articles.headline: NFL Hall of Famer Marshall Faulk, 53, Says He’s Been Diagnosed with Parkinson’s Disease
keyFacts: NFL Hall of Famer Marshall Faulk said he was diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease after noticing hand rigidity while playing golf.
Faulk stated that he has experienced mild symptoms for about a year and a half and continues to work as a football coach.
Faulk urged anyone with potential symptoms to consult a doctor, stating that early detection improves the quality of life.
body: Marshall Faulk in March 2026
Credit: Raj Mehta/Getty NEED TO KNOW
NFL legend Marshall Faulk said he was diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease
The Pro Football Hall of Famer said in a Wednesday, Oct. 21 podcast interview that he was diagnosed after noticing “rigidity” in his hand while playing golf
The 53-year-old, who is now coaching Southern University’s football team, said anyone who thinks they may have symptoms of the disease should tell their doctor and get tested
Marshall Faulk said he has been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease .

The Pro Football Hall of Famer, 53, shared the news with The Caring Neurologist host Dr. Sandeep Thakkar on Wednesday, Oct. 21. Faulk said he has been dealing with the disease for about a year and a half and has not been experiencing symptoms beyond hand rigidity and “little tremors” so far.

Faulk was diagnosed after noticing “rigidity” in his hand while playing golf. When the symptoms kept showing even when he wasn’t holding a golf club, Faulk decided he had to tell his doctor during a physical. His doctor immediately suggested that he get it checked by a specialist.
Faulk, who admitted to being “anal” about his health, said he wasn’t playing around.
“You tell me that and I’m going, like, I believe in going to the doctor,” the Southern University football coach told Thakkar.

The former running back said he doesn’t see Parkinson’s as “terminal,” recalling how he met Muhammad Ali after the boxing legend was diagnosed with the disease and seeing how Ali was “all there.” He also brought up actor Michael J. Fox , who has lived with Parkinson’s since 1991 .

“So, knowing that, I didn’t look at it like if I got a diagnosis, life was going to end,” Faulk said. “I treat it like -- I’ve had a bunch of surgeries on my right knee. There’s some parts in it that aren’t mine, that aren’t original. My back, you know, it hurts every once in a while.”

“It’s something you live with,” Faulk continued. “It’s not to where it’s a detriment to your livelihood. Now, if you don’t take care of it, there’s an opportunity for that to be. But you have to take care of it.”
Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now!
Parkinson’s disease is a neurodegenerative disorder affecting movement, according to the Parkinson’s Foundation . Its cause remains unknown and there is no cure.
Faulk hopes that by sharing his story, more people are encouraged to get checked by a trained specialist when they have concerns.

“The earlier you catch it, the better chance you have at living a better quality of life with medication compared to if you catch it later, the things that you start to have, the things that you go through, it makes life a little bit more difficult,” Faulk said.

Later in his discussion with Thakkar, Faulk said he hasn’t “really had the conversation” with his friends and family about his diagnosis, but he will “if it comes to a time where my lifestyle changes.”
Marshall Faulk in 2002
Credit: Sports Illustrated via Getty “I’m functioning. I’m good. You know, I just think I caught it early,” he said. “I’m in a good place.”

Faulk, who won a Super Bowl with the St. Louis Rams in 2000 and retired from the NFL in 2007, was hired as head football coach at Southern University in Baton Rouge, La. in December 2025. He was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame during his first year of eligibility in 2011.

articles.headline: What time is the World Series today? TV schedule, channel to watch Brewers vs. Rays games
keyFacts: The Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays will play in the 2026 World Series.
Every game of the series will begin at 8 p.m. ET and 7 p.m. CT.
The games will be broadcast exclusively on Fox and available on select streaming and radio platforms.
body: The 2026 World Series is set, with the best of the American League ready to take on the best of the National League.

The Milwaukee Brewers finally won the NL pennant, making the World Series for the first time in 44 years after a franchise-best 103 wins in the regular season. Led by manager Pat Murphy, the Brewers have a very balanced team with stars like Jackson Chourio and Jacob Misiorowski ready to take the big stage.

However, the Brewers will have to go through the Tampa Bay Rays, another team looking for its first-ever World Series championship. Kevin Cash's team is headlined by Junior Caminero, Yandy Diaz and Drew Rasmussen and won 98 games in the regular season.
Milwaukee will have home-field advantage, but both these fan bases are excited for a potentially franchise-altering series.
The Sporting News has you covered on all you need to know about how to watch and listen to every game of the World Series.
What time is the World Series today?
- Time: 8 p.m. ET, 7 p.m CT
Every game in the World Series will begin at 8:00 p.m. ET, 7:00 p.m. CT live from either American Family Field in Milwaukee or Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg.
How to watch Brewers vs. Rays World Series

The World Series between the Brewers and Rays will be broadcast exclusively on Fox with Joe Davis and John Smoltz on the call. Fans looking for an alternate streaming option can also find the game on DIRECTV or Fubo, both of which offer free trials.
Brewers vs. Rays radio station
- Radio station: SiriusXM Channels 202 (Rays), 203 (Brewers)
SiriusXM will have the radio broadcast of all World Series games between the Brewers and Rays. Fans can find the Rays broadcast on channel 202 and the Brewers broadcast on channel 203.

articles.headline: ‘Slow news day at the office’: LeBron James shrugs off Trump’s national anthem attack
keyFacts: Donald Trump criticized LeBron James on Truth Social for making warm-up movements during the national anthem before a game.
LeBron James dismissed the criticism after a game, stating that it must be a slow news day.
Philadelphia 76ers coach Nick Nurse stated that Trump's comments were outside noise that the team needed to tune out.
body: Donald Trump lashed out at NBA superstar LeBron James on Thursday for what he called disrespectful behavior during the playing of the national anthem.
Trump posted a video of the basketball legend making apparent warm-up movements while lined up with his Philadelphia 76ers teammates before their season opener against the New York Knicks on Tuesday.
“While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country! I said right from the beginning that he’s no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social network.
“LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!” he wrote.
The video used by Trump had an on-screen caption that read: “LeBron working on his golf swing pregame.” It showed him making lateral swinging motions and basketball shooting movements.
Trump, speaking at a campaign rally in Iowa on Thursday night, renewed the attack, calling James’s actions “a big scandal kind of a story”.
Trump and James have traded barbs before, and the NBA’s all-time leading scorer shrugged off the president’s latest criticism.
“It must be a slow news day at the office,” he said after the Sixers completed an epic comeback to beat the Cleveland Cavaliers 114-106 in Philadelphia. “Slow news day at the office.”
James, 41, is entering a record-extending 24th NBA season with his fourth team.
Sixers coach Nick Nurse said Trump’s comments were the kind of distractions he was schooling his team to tune out.

“I think that goes right in with other outside noise we’ve already had,” Nurse said. “I keep saying the same thing. All I really care about is getting to the practice floor, getting them in the film room, getting them to the game floor.
“The focus that they’ve had and the intent and all the stuff like that has been outstanding.”
Philadelphia’s win on Thursday marked both the largest comeback by the Sixers in the play-by-play era (since 1996-97) and the largest comeback win of James’s career.

James finished with 17 points, 10 rebounds, five assists and three steals, while Tyrese Maxey powered the rally with 32 points and a crucial defensive effort on James Harden. Jaylen Brown, also making his home debut in a 76ers uniform, scored 17 of his 21 points in the second half and 10 in the fourth quarter.
Trump has been critical of athletes before – particularly Black athletes – for their behavior during the playing of the Star-Spangled Banner before games.
During his first term, Trump singled out NFL star Colin Kaepernick for his decision to kneel during the Star-Spangled Banner to protest against racial injustice and police brutality.

articles.headline: Oura sues rival Ultrahuman again, threatening its U.S. smart ring comeback
keyFacts: Smart ring maker Oura filed a federal lawsuit against rival Ultrahuman, seeking to block U.S. sales of the Ring Pro and demanding monetary damages.
Oura alleged in the court filing that Ultrahuman infringes two of its patents covering the ring's design, battery, and internal sensors.
The legal action follows a previous import ban on Ultrahuman's earlier Ring Air after an International Trade Commission ruling secured by Oura.
body: Smart ring maker Oura has sued Indian rival Ultrahuman again, seeking to block U.S. sales of its Ring Pro (pictured above) just months after the redesign helped the Bengaluru-based startup return to the American market following an import ban. The case is the latest in a string of patent disputes Oura has brought against competing smart-ring makers, including Samsung and RingConn.

In a complaint filed Thursday in a federal court in Texas, Oura alleged that Ultrahuman’s Ring Pro infringes two of its patents covering the ring’s design and internal components, including its battery and sensors. Oura is seeking monetary damages and a permanent injunction that would stop Ultrahuman from selling the ring.

Ultrahuman’s redesigned Ring Pro, launched in February, received a favorable ruling from U.S. Customs and Border Protection in March, paving the way for the startup’s return to the U.S. market. The decision followed an import ban on Ultrahuman’s earlier Ring Air, which took effect after Oura secured a patent infringement ruling from the International Trade Commission in August last year.

“Ultrahuman has a history of copying Oura’s innovations, as demonstrated by the 2025 ITC ruling against the company,” an Oura spokesperson said in a statement to TechCrunch. “Ultrahuman introduced a redesigned ring but failed to address continued infringement of Oura’s patents, seeking instead to capitalize on our innovation and the market leadership we have built.”

Oura argues that the Customs ruling covered only the patent involved in the earlier dispute, not the two patents cited in its latest lawsuit: D804,471 and 12,769,363. “To protect its patent rights, Oura is now forced to file this complaint of patent infringement,” the company said in its filing.

One of those patents, 12,769,363, is also very new. It was issued to Oura on October 20, just two days before it filed the lawsuit. It covers a smart-ring design incorporating internal components such as a curved battery, circuit board, magnets, and sensors.

Oura has also named Texas-based electronics manufacturer SVTronics as a defendant in the lawsuit. The complaint says SVTronics manufactures the Ring Pro at a facility in Plano, Texas, allegedly under Ultrahuman’s direction and control. It also alleges that both companies infringe Oura’s patents through the manufacture, importation, and sale of the device in the U.S.

Oura and Ultrahuman have been fighting over patents since 2023, when Oura sued the Indian startup over its Ring Air, which had helped Ultrahuman make a name for itself in the U.S. Oura brought a separate case before the U.S. International Trade Commission in 2024 that helped it secure a ruling last year, leading to the import ban on the Ring Air.

Ultrahuman is not the only rival facing legal pressure from Oura. The company has also pursued patent infringement claims against smart-ring makers including Samsung, RingConn, Circular, and Zepp Health. Some of those disputes have ended in licensing agreements, with RingConn and Circular agreeing to pay royalties to Oura to continue selling their products.

The dispute emerges as the smart-ring market continues to grow. Research firm IDC expects global shipments to rise 12.8% this year to 4.9 million units and reach about 6.3 million by 2030. While Oura remains a leading player in the category, Ultrahuman is among the growing competitors.

The lawsuit also comes just weeks after Oura shelved its $2.2 billion IPO, citing “uncertainty” in the market. The company has continued to add features to its smart rings, introducing new fitness metrics earlier this week that help users track how workouts affect their cardiovascular health.

In September, Ultrahuman raised $70 million from investors including Qualcomm Ventures and Labcorp, valuing the startup at about $365 million. The startup is also working with Qualcomm on a new smart ring that could run more software directly on the device, as it looks to expand beyond health and fitness tracking into areas such as AI interactions and gaming.
Ultrahuman did not respond to a request for comment.

articles.headline: Israel arrests 36 Palestinians in the West Bank, attacks on farmers ramp up
keyFacts: Israeli forces arrested 36 Palestinians during raids across the occupied West Bank, according to Palestinian sources.
The Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission documented 17 attacks by Israeli forces and settlers on Palestinian farmers on Thursday.
The Israeli military briefly detained US Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander while he was helping Palestinian farmers harvest olives.
body: Israeli forces have arrested 36 Palestinians during raids across the occupied West Bank, as attacks on Palestinian farmers and their lands during the olive harvest season ramp up.
In Jenin governorate, Israeli forces raided towns and villages on Thursday, arresting 10 Palestinians, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported, citing data from the Palestinian Prisoner’s Society.
Israeli forces also raided the town of Tuqu in the Hebron governorate on Thursday and arrested former prisoner Shorok al-Badan, along with five others from other parts of Hebron, according to Wafa.

The Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission said on Thursday that Israeli forces arrested 14 people in Khirbet Jawaya village of Masafer Yatta in Hebron, while Wafa reported that three other Palestinians were arrested across the Hebron governorate, citing a security source.
In Nablus and Jerusalem, three more Palestinians were arrested during Israeli raids in the village of Burin, the town of Awarta, and the Qalandiya refugee camp.
Attack pattern
The Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission said it documented 17 pogroms by Israeli forces and settlers on Thursday against Palestinian farmers and their land during the olive harvest.
The incidents were recorded across occupied West Bank governorates, including Hebron, Qalqilya, Nablus, Ramallah and el-Bireh, Jenin and Salfit.

According to the Commission, the attacks included assaults on farmers, preventing them from reaching their land, theft of crops and agricultural equipment, damage and burning of olive trees, as well as arrests, threats at gunpoint and live fire.
The Commission says the pattern represents an escalation in attacks targeting the olive harvest and undermines Palestinians’ ability to access and cultivate their land and maintain their livelihoods.

Israeli attacks on Palestinian farmers garnered international attention and condemnation. US Democratic congressional candidate Brad Lander was briefly detained on Wednesday by the Israeli military with a warning while volunteering to help Palestinian farmers harvest olives in the occupied West Bank.

articles.headline: Trump says it’s ‘not looking good’ for Ilhan Omar — suggests she should be forced out of Congress for using ‘fake name’
keyFacts: President Trump stated Thursday that Rep. Ilhan Omar should resign from Congress if she used a false name to take office.
Federal court filings in an immigration fraud probe referred to the Minnesota Democrat by the surname Elmi instead of Omar.
Representatives for Omar did not immediately respond to requests for comment regarding the allegations.
body: President Trump signaled Thursday that he expects Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) to get the boot from Congress if it turns out that she used a “fake name” when she was sworn in.

“It’s not looking good,” Trump said of Omar’s legal predicament after bombshell court filings related to the federal immigration fraud probe against the congresswoman revealed her actual surname – Elmi – is identical to that of her ex-husband, who is also rumored to be her biological brother.
“She used a fake name to be sworn in,” Trump asserted at a rally in Iowa. “I assume she must immediately have to resign from Congress.”

The president directed rally-goers to “please inform our great Speaker of the House of Representatives … that the Democrat Party has just conceded her seat. That Ilhan Nur Said Elmi, her real name, has openly admitted to fraud, and she will not be legally allowed to be a member of that august body any longer.”
“She won’t be able,” he continued. “I mean, I don’t know: If you get sworn in with a false name, I would imagine that’s pretty tough to remain.”
Prosecutors referred to the Minnesota Democrat as “Ilhan Nur Said Elmi, a/k/a Ilhan Abdullahi Omar,” in a Wednesday filing in DC federal court.
A source familiar with the investigation confirmed that Omar is not the congresswoman’s “real” last name, meaning she was born with the last name of Elmi.
Reps for Omar did not immediately respond to The Post’s request for comment.
Trump also mocked Omar’s less-than-forceful denial that her ex-husband, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, may be a blood relative.
“Not to my knowledge,” Omar responded when asked directly on MS NOW on Wednesday whether she was related to her former husband.
Trump called it “one of the worst answers I think I’ve ever heard.”
“You know I’ve heard some bad political answers … but that would be about the worst,” the president said, arguing that Omar “didn’t know whether or not she married her brother.”
Trump, who has long been critical of Omar, went on to call her a “scammer.”
“I’m pretty good at watching that stuff, and she’s been a scammer for a long time,” he said.
Earlier this week, the president suggested Omar could face jail time if convicted of immigration fraud.
“She could go to jail,” Trump said Tuesday. “They keep talking about deportation.”
The Minnesota Democrat maintains she became a citizen at age 17 through her father, who became a naturalized citizen in 2000, five years after emigrating to the US.
She has vehemently denied any wrongdoing.
During the rally, Trump also announced plans to use federal dollars to expand domestic diesel and gasoline production.

“In more breaking news, my administration is using the Defense Production Act to release $150 million to increase American refining capacity to produce more diesel and more gasoline at record levels,” the president said.
In a statement, Energy Secretary Chris Wright said the funds “will be used strategically and in partnership with private industry to rapidly bolster America’s existing energy infrastructure.”
“By restoring energy addition policies, we will continue to unleash American energy dominance and lower costs for the American people,” Wright added.

articles.headline: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 review – It’s good to see you again
keyFacts: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 offers three deep modes of play following a development cycle of over three years.
The game features a campaign with high stakes and mission variety, alongside an extraction shooter mode called DMZ.
The multiplayer component returns to a boots-on-the-ground realism style of movement while sparking ongoing debate regarding skill-based matchmaking.
body: Call of Duty . I know you well after 20 years of this franchise, but you can still surprise me.

My career as a journalist began with CoD all the way back in college. My senior thesis in journalism school was a 10,000-word magazine piece about the franchise in the early 2010s, because it was my obsession at the time. Since then, I’ve played and experienced all there is to offer with varying levels of enjoyment and satisfaction, so it’s been hard not to feel a general level of fatigue with the yearly releases.

But still, every once in a while, the franchise is capable of greatness despite the wear and tear. Modern Warfare 4 is the latest and best example of this, offering three distinct modes of play that are all deep and well-made, and worth the price of admission this year.

The biggest takeaway from this year’s CoD is that, given the time needed to create a full-fledged game with multiple dedicated modes without having to rush another game out the door, Infinity Ward (and its multiple partnered CoD studios under Activision) is still more than capable of using three-plus years of dev time to create a good and varied experience.
Lines crossed, lines held

Image via Activision While CoD may have built its empire on multiplayer greatness, MW4 shows that a good campaign goes a long way. And this is far and away the franchise’s best in recent years, and one of the greatest in franchise history.

MW4 closes out the story of the MW reboot trilogy in epic, dramatic, and emotional fashion. Mission variety and high stakes are complemented by excellent visuals and sound design, and a narrative that feels worthy of the characters and story that people have come to love.

Captain Price is out for revenge. North Korea attacks South Korea and throws a squad of new and interesting soldiers into the mix. Ghost and Gaz are tasked with a difficult mission, leading to some epic fan-service. It’s really well-done throughout, especially when it comes to the standards of CoD campaigns in recent years, carried further by excellent performances from its cast.

I wrote at length about MW4’s campaign last week , but to put it succinctly, it’s a great experience, albeit a short one. And it’s been awesome to see most players agree, experiencing the campaign in early access before full launch and enjoying all it has to offer.

One controversial mission in the game opens it up to an open-world scenario, similar to previous campaigns, but I felt it was done very well this time. Playing as a South Korean soldier behind enemy lines in North Korea, you’re forced to scavenge, survive, and complete objectives to save your squad that’s out of commission. I found it as a nice change of pace from the rest of the campaign’s standard corridor set pieces, and given that most of it can be skipped/sped through if you wish to do so, I don’t mind it at all.
Risky rewards

Image via Activision On the heels of the popularity of games like ARC Raiders and Escape From Tarkov, CoD returns with its own variant on the extraction shooter with DMZ , and it basically functions as a fully fleshed-out extraction shooter within MW4 on top of its other offerings.

DMZ’s Beta in Modern Warfare II four years ago was more of a sandbox and proof of concept. This time around, it’s got its own dedicated progression, multiple methods of play, story missions, an explorable home base, and it feels designed to keep players invested in the long haul.

Visiting Infinity Ward HQ and playing DMZ within the studio brought a lot of insight into the mode, and it’s very positive. I mentioned in my impressions of DMZ earlier this week that I think it has massive potential, but in the end I think it will come down to how PvE, PvP, and PvEvP are balanced. This feels especially important as MW4 is the first CoD in many years without a third mode dedicated entirely to PvE (like Zombies or Spec Ops), and some players are already calling for PvE-exclusive experiences in DMZ .

At launch, DMZ feels like a mostly PvE-centric experience as players learn the ropes, with PvP encounters taking a backseat thus far. Some players may love it, while the sweaty Warzone gamers who want to treat it like battle royale may be scared off if they can’t actively find other squads to wipe throughout each 30-minute match. Trying to keep many subsets of players happy is one of the biggest struggles of a CoD dev, and now it’s set to take place in an extraction shooter where losing a gunfight might mean losing dozens of hours of progress or more. I wish them luck with that.

DMZ will continue to take shape over the course of the next few months, with Infinity Ward (along with its partners Beenox, Digital Legends, Activision Shanghai, Raven Software, Treyarch, Sledgehammer Games, and High Moon Studios who all worked on different aspects of MW4 ) keeping a close eye on how things are going down within the exclusion zone in the fictional location of Hajin. Season one adds a new endgame-style map, and season two unlocks the northern part of the map that includes Russia. Couple that with new weapons and gear every month or so, and there should be plenty to keep players busy if the mode scratches an extraction itch.
Mainstay, madness

Image via Activision And then we have the multiplayer component. Love it or hate it (I’ve experienced both feelings throughout the series), CoD’s multiplayer is often what keeps people coming back throughout seasonal releases for new maps, new modes, new weapons, unlockable camos, and more. And keeping with tradition, MW4’s multiplayer experience is already set to be polarizing.

Bucking the trend of the past two games, MW4’s multiplayer brings it back to a more boots-on-the-ground realism style of movement, ditching the omnimovement and wall-jumping found in Black Ops 6 and 7 . It’s a welcome change, and should even the playing field a bit for players who dislike the wildness of “movement demons,” as they are not-so-lovingly called online.

The base experience of MW4’s multiplayer is solid. The gunplay feels fun, and the movement is still CoD -like but with less ridiculousness than the futuristic games offer, as players can still do things like mantle quickly over obstacles, slide and dive, and jump-shot their way to victory in gunfights.

Traditionally, map design defines the CoD multiplayer experience, and those available at launch are hit-or-miss so far (plus there’s only 12 of them), so I’m hoping to see some variety among seasonal releases, with some new additions likely joining remade classics such as Shipment and more.

There’s also a metric ton of challenges and unlocks to keep players busy for months, and several new modes are quite fun. While playing at Infinity Ward, I especially enjoyed the new Counter-Strike / VALORANT -like mode Collateral, and Gunfight on the evolving map called Kill Block. But the main question with CoD multiplayer over the past decade or so is if you can retain your sanity long enough to keep up the joy.

Once again, the CoD multiplayer discussion is set to be dominated by skill-based matchmaking. This is unfortunate, because the gameplay itself is pretty strong, so I’m mainly plagued with worries and questions about how everything will shake out over seasonal content drops and balancing updates.

Treyarch opened Pandora’s box last year by changing up the formula and testing matchmaking playlists of different varieties where skill is less of a consideration, such as the Open matchmaking style. It felt great for a while, but it’s still an evolving situation, as ever. And now Infinity Ward has been a bit mum on the subject thus far, which is a potential cause for concern, but at launch, Open matchmaking is nowhere to be found. A big disappointment.

Image via Activision According to Activision, skill has to be something of a factor in multiplayer matchmaking, for a variety of reasons that the company says it determined by studying player behavior has gone into in the past. But it feels like you’re actively being punished for being halfway decent at the game by getting matched up against a god-squad after a match where you put up some good numbers, it can really kill the vibe. Worries and my own personal frustrations as an aging gamer aside, the base multiplayer experience feels fun, but could easily be an issue for those who feel filtered out or punished by SBMM.

Over the next year, updates could make or break how MW4 is remembered as a CoD game by its most fervent players. But as a day one experience, all three of its modes feel representative of the time and care that went into them, marking this as one of the better entries in the franchise in recent memory.
The post Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 review – It’s good to see you again appeared first on Destructoid .

articles.headline: I tested my Apple Watch Ultra 4 against Casio's cheap step-counting retro watch, the Casio F-B100W
keyFacts: TechRadar tested the step-tracking accuracy of the budget Casio F-B100W watch against the expensive Apple Watch Ultra 4.
The author reported that the Casio watch recorded 4,641 steps during a run, while the Apple Watch recorded 4,679 steps.
The author concluded that the Casio watch is just as effective a step counter as the Apple Watch despite the massive price difference.
body: If you've been following TechRadar's fitness coverage over the last couple of months, you'll have heard about the Casio F-B100W.

It's a cheap Bluetooth digital watch — ($65 / £55 / AU$119) and despite looking very similar to the classic, extremely cheap F-91W, it's got some differences. It's a little bit bigger, it's got an additional button, a dual time-zone mode, and, crucially for our purposes, a few smart features thanks to its Bluetooth capability: Find My Phone, and a step tracker.

This stripped-back approach to smartwatches is great for people who are looking to increase their activity levels, but don't want to pay for a smartwatch or use all the bells and whistles of a full-fledged fitness tracker. In fact, it reminds me of the very first Fitbits, which were simple pebble-shaped Bluetooth-enabled step trackers that clipped to your clothes.

I had a lot of fun with this watch, as I loved the retro styling, and it had just enough smarts to be useful. As a perpetual phone-misplacer, Find My Phone functionality is an essential for me for any smartwatch, while the most basic movement-based metric of step tracking remains useful even today. In the app, your step counts are broken into bar charts over a week, month or year to analyze trends.

But, considering the extraordinary cheap price of the watch, I was wondering how accurate it could be. So I decided to test it against this year's best smartwatch, the Apple Watch Ultra 4. The Ultra 4 costs $799 / £749 / AU$1,349, a far cry from the cost of the Casio, and is equipped with top-of-the-range fitness metrics for every eventuality.

To start with, it's worth noting that I can't separate the Casio's daily step counter into a specific workout, so by the time I'd strapped both watches on, and gone up and down the stairs putting my shoes on, finding my keys and earphones, and stepping out to the starting point of my run, I had already walked 269 steps, and that was reflected in the Casio's score. Not the best start to the experiment.

However, after the run was complete, I checked the scores on both apps immediately. Once the Apple Watch's workout was marked as 'complete' it stopped tracking my steps, so I didn't want to make the same mistake again and inflate the Casio's score. The moment I finished my workout on the Apple Watch, I screenshotted both apps.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
And I was impressed. The Casio recorded a score of 4,910 steps. Minus my initial 269 steps, that leaves us at 4,641 steps in total for the Casio F-B100W.

The Apple Watch Ultra 4 recorded 4,679, a difference of just 38 steps. That's a teeny margin of error for two completely different watches in two completely different price brackets, operating solely on estimations from their onboard sensors, and I'm thrilled with this result.

What does this mean in practice? It means that if all you're interested in is tracking your steps, and you like the retro digital watch vibe (after all, retro tech has been making a comeback for a while now) I can say that the humble Casio F-B100W was just as good a step counter as the most expensive Apple Watch on the market, and I can double-down on my recommendation. It's a great watch.

Admittedly, it doesn't have the other advanced metrics of the Apple Watch (or any other metrics, for that matter), but this test was an exercise in testing the Casio step counter's quality, not objectively comparing the two watches — and it passed that test with flying colors.

articles.headline: At least 16 dead when powerful 7.0 magnitude earthquake strikes Tibet
keyFacts: At least 16 people died and 54 were injured when a magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Tibet on Thursday evening, local officials said.
The disaster destroyed at least 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds in a sparsely populated area of northern Tibet, according to the Nagqu media office.
More than 1,600 people were deployed for search and rescue efforts, and emergency supplies arrived in the region.
body: More than a dozen people were killed and hundreds of homes destroyed when a magnitude 7.0 earthquake hit China's Tibet region on Thursday evening local time, according to local officials.

The United States Geological Survey said the quake occurred at 10:33 p.m. local time, with its epicenter 119 miles east-northeast of Nagqu, in a sparsely populated, high-altitude area of northern Tibet.
At least 16 people were killed and 54 people were injured in the earthquake, Chinese state media said.

Search and rescue efforts continued following the collapse of at least 339 homes and 20 livestock sheds, the Nagqu media office said, citing city government officials. Among the injured, 11 people were in serious condition and the other 35 sustained minor injuries, the media office said.

More than 1,600 people from the local county were deployed for rescue efforts. Supplies including 1,000 prefabricated housing units, around 3,000 tents and folding beds, as well as flashlights and winter clothing arrived in the region.
It was the biggest earthquake in the region in the last five years, China's national broadcaster CCTV said.
Nagqu is more than 186 miles north of Tibet's capital, Lhasa.
The USGS put the earthquake's depth at 11 miles. Xinhua, citing the China Earthquake Networks Center, put the depth at 6.2 miles.
The earthquake comes less than two months after a border region of Nepal and Tibet that left hundreds of people dead and . Authorities said was caused by the collapse of a glacier.

articles.headline: House Freedom Caucus trashes Axios report on internal rift over Brandon Gill
keyFacts: The House Freedom Caucus rejected an Axios report claiming some members want Rep. Brandon Gill out.

Rep. Brandon Gill has not responded to the report as of Thursday night.
body: The House Freedom Caucus is directly rejecting a new Axios report that claims some members within the group want Rep. Brandon Gill (R-TX) out.

A small group in the caucus is allegedly unhappy with the 32-year-old freshman lawmaker as he continues building his national profile during the midterm elections , Axios reported on Thursday without naming the disgruntled caucus members.
But for those who were glad to have Gill on board, they publicly complained that the news outlet didn’t quote them.

“Here’s what I said on the record that they didn’t print,” Rep. Ralph Norman (R-SC) said on X before posting the statement. “Brandon Gill is proving exactly why he belongs in the Freedom Caucus. While the media invents division with anonymous sources, Gill is out there dismantling Leftist myths and rooting out corruption. The Caucus is locked in and laser-focused on the SAVE America Act, securing our border, and stopping the radicals who want to destroy this country.”
Another House Freedom Caucus member specifically labeled Axios “fake news” for publishing the story based on anonymous sources.
“I spoke to this reporter on the record for this story, and of course no mention of what I said,” Rep. Eli Crane (R-AZ) wrote . “More fake news. [Gill] is awesome.”
The caucus called the article “absurd” on social media while praising Gill as a “rising star” in its ranks.

“The media is so desperate to distract from socialists taking over the Democrat party that they’re ginning up anonymous-source hit pieces on Republicans less than 2 weeks before the Midterms,” the conservative hard-line group said . “Don’t fall for the phony manufactured drama.”
Even Rep. Riley Moore (R-WV), who is not a member of the House Freedom Caucus, rushed to Gill’s defense, calling him a “patriot and a huge asset to our conference.”
As of Thursday night, Gill has not responded to the report himself.
BRANDON GILL’S VIRAL RISE FUELS POTENTIAL BID FOR TOP HOUSE OVERSIGHT ROLE

The Texas Republican has been busy campaigning for reelection, raising nearly $4.7 million in the third quarter alone. Gill’s office said he has donated to the campaigns of over a dozen of his fellow House Freedom Caucus members, Axios noted. He has also contributed $1.1 million to the National Republican Congressional Committee, trying to grow his influence within the broader House Republican Conference.

Gill launched a bid for the top seat on the House oversight committee after Rep. James Comer (R-KY) announced he would step down as its chairman at the end of his term. Gill’s ambition appears to be a friction point with other Republicans.

articles.headline: Serbia: Tens of thousands rally ahead of elections
keyFacts: Tens of thousands of Serbians rallied in Belgrade on Thursday for the final campaign event ahead of a pivotal election against President Aleksandar Vucic.
The anti-corruption protest movement, led by university students, emerged following a 2024 railway station canopy collapse that killed 16 people.
Analysts warn that a close election result could lead to post-election instability if both sides declare victory.
body: Over a hundred thousand of Serbians took to the streets in support of Serbia's protesting youth movement on Thursday, in what was the final campaign rally ahead of a pivotal election challenge to the Balkan nation's populist strongman, Aleksandar Vucic.

Crowds poured into Belgrade's central square from all directions and filled up several blocks around the area. Independent crowd-monitoring group Archive of Public Gatherings estimated about 150,000 people were at the rally.

The optimistic crowds chanted "victory" ahead of Sunday's crunch vote which comes after two years of student-led protests against Vucic. It was triggered by a 2024 collapse of a canopy at the newly renovated Novi Sad railway station which killed 16 people.
The anti-corruption movement, led by university students, has since snowballed from demands for an independent investigation into the incident, into calls for early elections.
What happened at the protest?
The Student List, a leaderless movement of student-backed candidates, is the veteran leader's biggest threat.
Thousands supporting it flocked to Belgrade's streets on Thursday.

"I came to support the Student List because young people finally gave me hope that it is possible to live in a normal country," 47-year-old Marija Nedeljkovic Radic told the French AFP news agency as she arrived for the students' rally.
"Really, for the first time in my life, I believe that it is possible," she said.

"We are putting an end to 14 years of humiliation, chaos and betrayal, and to decades of putting personal and party interests above yours," university professor Jugoslav Gasic, one of 250 candidates on the Student List, told the crowd who chanted "Victory, victory!"
"You deserve better, and we know how to deliver it. Students are winning!"
How has Vucic responded?
Vucic has dominated Serbian politics for over a decade now, either as prime minister or president of the Balkan country.
As pressure from the protests mounted, he announced a snap election last month. He has resigned as president, but many argue it is a tactical move so that he could run for prime minister.
This is now the biggest electoral challenge his party, the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), has faced since it was elected into power in 2012.
The leader, meanwhile, has regularly accused the students movement of being a foreign-funded coup.

"Let us never forget how they tried to bring down our state. Let us always protect and defend it," Vucic said to a sports hall full of supporters on Thursday. "Let us go out and defeat them! Defeat them decisively!"
Worries of post-result unrest
Days before the vote, Serbian civil societies warned that conditions for "free and fair election" were lacking.

"This assessment is not based on isolated incidents, opposition claims or political disagreement with the government," a joint statement by 24 organisations said, arguing it was supported by documented findings.

Analysts warn that a close election result could lead to post-election instability, if both sides declare victory. Vucic, who controls the Serbian police, has said he would quash any unrest after the vote.

While several minor parties are also in the race for premiership, observers say that there is a referendum-like atmosphere between Vucic and the students' movement which could sideline other parties in the 250-member parliament.

articles.headline: Arizona coach Tommy Lloyd has a theory: NCAA is embracing eligibility chaos to leverage federal legislation
keyFacts: Arizona coach Tommy Lloyd stated that the NCAA is intentionally embracing eligibility chaos to help promote federal legislation like the Protect College Sports Act.
Lloyd noted that the NCAA is currently fighting legal battles over player eligibility instead of issuing blanket waivers as it did previously after the Diego Pavia case.
The ongoing legal disputes and inconsistent judge rulings have created an uneven playing field and distracted from the upcoming college basketball season.
body: KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- When I sat down with Tommy Lloyd this week here inside the T-Mobile Center during what amounted to the second half of Big 12 Media Days, I expected to talk to the Arizona coach about everything from his rejection of North Carolina to the additions of Caleb Holt and Cameron Holmes.
I figured Ivan Kharchenkov might come up. Perhaps even Bryce James.
But Diego Pavia?

The former Vanderbilt quarterback/future UFL player was nowhere in my notes. But Lloyd is coming off of a Final Four, in charge of one of college basketball's biggest brands, and an obviously smart guy. So before I was done with our conversation about his program and team, I wanted to get his thoughts about A) Kansas recently, and controversially, enrolling a 24-year-old who was the 59th pick in June's NBA Draft (Trey Kaufman-Renn), B) the NCAA relentlessly challenging five-year-eligibility-period cases connected to 2022 high school graduates, and C) everything else taking up so much oxygen in the sport of college basketball these days.
So I did.
Then the conversation got really good.

"My stance on the 5-for-5 is very clear," Lloyd began. "If you're a true 5-for-5 [case], and if the same situation were next year, and you could be eligible without a waiver, you shouldn't be ineligible now. [But] if you're in your sixth or seventh year [of college], and if you've got a story and a bunch of extenuating circumstances, yeah, I'm not too sympathetic to that. So I think what's frustrating for me is [that] when you kind of take a step back and you think about all of the conversations that go on behind the scenes, and, you know, we could go through a few of them here ..."
Lloyd trailed off there for a moment.

"The Pavia Case" is where he picked up before explaining the different ways in which the NCAA is handling things now compared to how it handled them just two years ago when Pavia sued the governing body while arguing that its rules counting his junior college seasons against his Division I eligibility violated the Sherman Antitrust Act by improperly limiting his career and ability to earn name, image, and likeness income potentially worth millions of dollars.
Pavia won his case.

His college football career continued thanks to an injunction. Not long after it was granted, the NCAA Division I Board of Directors approved a blanket waiver granting an extra year of eligibility for the 2025-26 academic year to former JUCO and non-NCAA school transfers who were in a position similar to Pavia's.

"[After the Pavia case], the NCAA ... released a memo to the schools that [more or less said], 'based on this single ruling, we see it can create an uneven playing field among our competitive schools, so we are going to issue a blanket waiver for any kid that's basically in the same circumstances that Pavia was in.' And they did a blanket waiver."
Lloyd's point?

Why isn't the NCAA issuing a blanket waiver now, considering there are men set to play college basketball in less than two weeks only because they received injunctions from local judges just like Pavia once did? Why isn't the NCAA issuing a blanket waiver now while acknowledging that not doing so would create an unequal playing field based on which players get injunctions and which don't, given that the NCAA did exactly that two years ago after acknowledging that not doing so would, yes, create an unequal playing field based on which players get injunctions and which don't?
Those seem like totally reasonable questions. I asked Lloyd if he had an answer to them/theory about them.
Lloyd's theory: Chaos may be the point

"I think I do," he answered. "I think my theory is this thing has gotten so political -- and, obviously, there are a lot of things that need to be fixed in college sports," Lloyd said. "So [in my opinion,] the NCAA doesn't mind the 'chaos' right now because it can help drive the case for them to promote the [Protect] College Sports Act, which I'm sure we need."

(Translation: The NCAA desperately wants the PCSA to pass ASAP, and it's easier to make the case to the public that college sports needs saving when there are stories weekly about players being ruled eligible and ineligible by local judges for reasons that are inconsistent, confusing and often biased. More specifically, the NCAA's constant legal battles enhance the perception of "chaos" in college sports, which in turn makes it easier for senators like Ted Cruz to insist college sports needs "saving" via a federal law that, as currently constructed, would limit what athletes can make in a way that would otherwise likely be deemed illegal.)

Lloyd's explanation makes as much sense as, if not more sense than, anything anybody else has floated because, he's absolutely right, the NCAA is "digging its heels" in now in one case after another in ways that run completely counter to how it handled similar situations after Pavia's case two years ago.
Why?
Lloyd thinks the answer is italicized above. If you care, I agree.

Either way, Lloyd's larger point, and one I also co-sign, is that just because something might be a smart legal strategy, or a brilliant long-term play, that doesn't make it good or right. As the sixth-year Arizona coach noted, there are lots of men -- exactly 22 just in the Big 12 alone, by his count -- who would be eligible for a fifth year of eligibility if the NCAA's new five-year-eligibility-period rule would've been adopted earlier or if they'd just been born a little later. There's no real difference between them and many of the people we'll all watch play five years of college basketball moving forward or even this season. They were just born roughly a year earlier and enrolled in college when they did.

"Why should these individual kids [be punished and suffer] real damages?" Lloyd asked. "I mean, there have been guys that have come back for their fifth year and gotten drafted the next year because of that extra year of experience. And there [are players who are] going to make a lot of money [if they are eligible for a fifth year this season]. I mean, there's real damage [being suffered if they can't play this fifth year this season]. So, for me, somebody has to sit down and tell me why this makes sense and how it's good for the sport."
Players caught in the middle

Lloyd does have a so-called dog in this fight -- namely RJ Godfrey, who graduated high school in 2022, played three years at Clemson, one year at Georgia, graduated, and would now like to play a fifth year at Arizona. A judge in his home state of Georgia initially granted an injunction clearing Godfrey to play. But, more recently, the Georgia Court of Appeals granted the NCAA a stay, leaving Godfrey's future very much up in the air even though older players with less compelling eligibility cases are seemingly good to go thanks to how their legal cases have unfolded in different states with different judges.

"I get it's complicated -- but you can't tell me it's right that a true 5-for-5 [candidate] that's younger than some of these European players [is ineligible]," Lloyd continued. "[The only difference is] these European players, you know what they didn't do? They didn't redshirt. They [instead] played four years of high-level basketball [professionally] -- and just because they didn't enroll in a school, now they're getting [what amounts to] a [fifth] year of eligibility when our guy, or someone else's guy, enrolled, graduated in four years, and now they're getting penalized for a fifth year because they enrolled right when they graduated out of high school?
"It's just tough."
I'll take it a step further.

Not only would it obviously be unfair and inconsistent if, just to name one case, Trey Kaufman-Renn is allowed to spend a sixth year in a college basketball program and play a fifth this season while Godfrey and other younger players like him aren't allowed to spend a fifth literally in the same conference, all because of rulings by different judges in different places, I'd argue it's also counter-productive to what so many like to call the good of the game.

As I've noted many times on the Eye On College Basketball Podcast, do you realize the number of minutes Matt Norlander and I have spent talking about judges and injunctions this offseason instead of Florida attempting to win a second national title in three years or Jon Scheyer trying to get his first at Duke? Every second spent discussing court rulings is a second not spent on Vanderbilt's Tyler Tanner.
It's damaging to the sport.
I should've been talking to Tommy Lloyd about Motiejus Krivas. Instead, I talked to him about Diego Pavia.
Why?

Because the very sensible position the NCAA took two years ago after Pavia's ruling has been abandoned in a way that Lloyd and other coaches find inconsistent and frustrating -- and tied to ulterior motives. While the NCAA is spending millions of dollars fighting against players like Godfrey, most coaches would've preferred it grant a blanket waiver to every 2022 high school graduate, allow them to play a fifth year this season if they wanted to, and if anybody wanted them to, and just be done with it. Doing so would've saved a lot of legal fees and decreased the amount of so-called "chaos" dramatically. It's what coaches wanted -- evidence being Norlander and I asked roughly 100 of them earlier this year, and , if only to cut down on the confusion and level the playing field.

But rather than listen to the coaches, or even to the arguments the NCAA itself made just two years earlier about an uneven playing field after Pavia's ruling, the NCAA is out there fighting one legal battle after another, literally from coast to coast, at a cost that can't possibly be sensibly rationalized, all while creating the chaos it swears it wants to end.
It makes no sense -- unless the NCAA actually wants the chaos.

That's Lloyd's best explanation for what's going on -- going on still, with the season now just 10 days away -- that the NCAA has dug its heels in to fight, fight, fight this time around, in ways that are almost certainly going to create an uneven playing field this college basketball season, and in ways that totally contradict what the same governing body priortized just two years ago, not because its leaders or lawyers believe it's the right or logically consistent thing to do, but rather because it enhances the perception of "chaos" at a time when that perception, real or otherwise, might really be the thing that pushes a controversial bill through the senate and house and turns it into federal law.
"There's literally going to be an uneven playing field created [this season]" Lloyd said. "And the NCAA is letting it happen."

articles.headline: The Battlestar Galactica Board Game Is Making a Surprise Comeback Next Year
keyFacts: Ghost Galaxy agreed with Universal and Fantasy Flight Games to publish a new edition of Battlestar Galactica: The Board Game.
The out-of-print social deduction game will launch a crowdfunding campaign early next year with an updated design.
Christian T. Peterson, CEO of Ghost Galaxy and founder of Fantasy Flight Games, will oversee the project.
body: When it comes to board games, a frequent “Holy Grail” game (a term used to describe a game that someone has been hunting for, usually out of print and expensive) on many lists is Fantasy Flight Games’ Battlestar Galactica: The Board Game. But it looks like the search may be coming to an end for fans, as it was announced today that Ghost Galaxy has entered into an agreement with Universal and Fantasy Flight Games to publish a brand-new edition of this coveted title, coming to crowdfunding early next year.

First released back in 2008 and featuring imagery from the Sci-Fi Channel reboot , this social deduction/hidden traitor game wonderfully captured the tension from the show, where anyone could be a secret Cylon agent trying to thwart the single mission of the humans—to get home. Battlestar Galactica would go on to get three expansions, but almost a decade ago now, it all went out of print, and now prices on the secondary market for a full set (base game + expansions) could easily cost you more than a grand. Back in 2021, FFG did release a sort of reskinned version of BSG with Unfathomable, which replaced the Galactica with a boat and the Cylons with Lovecraftian horrors, which has seen success as well.

Details on this new edition are scant right now; all we have is that it’s a “new edition” that will feature “an updated design,” whatever that means, but I think the game is in safe hands. Overseeing this project will be Christian T. Peterson, the CEO of Ghost Galaxy and formerly the founder and CEO of Fantasy Flight Games and the creator of a little game called Twilight Imperium.

Recently, Fantasy Flight Games launched a similar campaign as the debut of its “Vault Series” with Arkham Horror Remastered (check out our interview and exclusive art reveal ), which seeks to accomplish a similar goal with the much-loved Arkham Horror Second Edition. Whether this will be a part of the Vault Series or not, seeing as it is being officially published by another group, remains to be seen, but awesome to hear nonetheless.
The campaign page for the new edition of Battlestar Galactica will be launching soon, so you and your wallet can rejoice.

body: A New Jersey Republican mayor charged toward a resident during a chaotic township council meeting this week and had to be physically restrained as he shouted threats at the man, dramatic video shows.
Pemberton Township Mayor Matthew Bianchini, a Republican, rushed toward the resident during Wednesday night's meeting before several people intervened and pulled him away.

The mayor acknowledged that his conduct was inappropriate.

"I should not have said that," he told the station. "That was wrong. It was in the heat of the moment. I'm not gonna get anybody."
The confrontation happened while a recently fired township employee was addressing the council.

articles.headline: GOP Candidate Confronted About Begging Supporters For Gas Money And Her Answer Says A Lot
keyFacts: Iowa Republican Senate candidate Ashley Hinson was questioned by NBC News about asking campaign supporters for gas money for her bus.
Hinson defended the request by stating she is actively campaigning across the state and listening to voters who are facing financial struggles.
During the same interview, Hinson stated she disagrees with Donald Trump regarding a diesel fuel deal with Russia.
body: The Republican candidate for U.S. Senate in Iowa, Ashley Hinson, was pressed during an interview with NBC News about a bizarre request she made to her supporters while breaking with President Donald Trump on a major issue.
Speaking with NBC News’ Tom Llamas on Wednesday, Hinson was asked about a recent statement she made requesting gas money from her supporters for the campaign’s bus.
“I just saw a report that said you were asking your supporters for gas money for your bus,” Llamas said before showing a clip from the campaign rally.

“I want you to channel ... into action in getting your friends out to vote, help give us a little gas money for our bus, make sure we’re showing up at the polls, because there is more to do,” Hinson said at the rally in Fort Dodge last week.
“I mean, is that how bad things are?” Llamas asked.

“No, I’m out there campaigning through the state on my bus, meeting with everyone where they are,” Hinson said. “And what I’m hearing from Iowans is that they want a leader, a commonsense mom who is going to focus on their priorities, because there are a lot of Iowans who are being priced out of the American dream. I understand that. I am focused on that.”
Despite seemingly obfuscating her answer, Hinson said she disagrees with Trump’s diesel fuel deal with Russia.

“I think that’s a bad idea. I don’t think we should be making deals with Russia. I do want to see the war come to an end as soon as possible. I want it to be successful,” Hinson said a day before Trump was set to campaign with her in Iowa on Thursday.
It should be noted that Hinson has voted five times against a War Powers Resolution to end the Iran war.

articles.headline: Etsy is cracking down on AI slop listings
keyFacts: Etsy announced stricter policies requiring the first photo of any listing to be an unedited image of the actual item.
Etsy stated the new rules aim to reduce misleading AI-generated content and platform listings made by bots.
Etsy noted that AI-generated art remains permitted if sellers properly disclose its use.
body: Etsy is announcing stricter rules about how AI can be used in listings to reduce the volume of AI slop on the platform. In a post, the company says that “many active buyers say they can’t tell which items involve AI-generated content” and that sellers are “concerned about your work appearing alongside items that use AI in misleading ways,” spurring the new policies and restrictions.
Etsy is cracking down on AI slop listings
Etsy’s new AI policies, among other changes, require that a listing’s first photo is unedited.

Under the new policies, every listing must include “at least one unedited photo of the actual item against a real background,” and all photos must “accurately represent the item a buyer will receive.” The photos that aren’t the first one can be edited with software or AI-powered tools, as long as “the final result remains an accurate representation of the physical product.” The company shared a few examples to demonstrate the type of misleading images that are prohibited, including the cat stuffed animal at the top of this post.

While uploading images for a listing, if Etsy detects that any may be AI-generated, the platform will show a pop-up where you can note if an image was made with AI or not, as shown in a video. If a buyer reports that what they receive is “materially different” from a listing, a seller may be responsible for a refund.

For sellers who offer “functional guides,” which include patterns, recipes, or instructions,” Etsy says that the information in those products “must be your own work, not generated by AI.” Sellers will have to show an “actual result” made from a guide. The company also says that listings made by bots are no longer allowed.
Selling AI-generated art is still allowed on the platform, but a seller must disclose that it was made with AI, Etsy says.

Max Verstappen revealed concerns over the state of his spine as he unleashed a scathing criticism of the "out of control" bumpy track surface at Circuit of The Americas.
The four-time world champion arrives in Austin for Sunday's United States Grand Prix after claiming his first two victories of the season in back-to-back races.
Speaking to the media on Thursday, Verstappen was unexpectedly passionate over the state of the circuit, which is generally considered as one of the most popular among the drivers on the F1 calendar.
"You see also the track state from what I saw in WEC (World Endurance Championship), it was extremely badly bumpy," Verstappen said.

"I'm not really looking forward to that to be honest, for your spine. I was joking about that in the last race but it's not really a joke to be honest because we mentioned this already for years that it's actually getting a bit out of control.
"I'm sure it's going to be quite tough to find the right compromises around this track in places where it's just extremely bumpy. I don't know how our car is going to respond to that."
The Red Bull driver appeared to be urging the event organisers to place greater emphasis on improving the surface for the event in future.
"Of course, you can use the excuse that the soil is the problem, but then you should have known that you need to make sure that you reinforce it more," Verstappen continued.
"I love this track. I love this place. It's one of the best layouts ever and it's one of the venues, best cities to be at. But for me, the bumps that we have are unacceptable.
"Over time, they've been grinding a little bit here and there, but it's just putting a plaster on the big problem - that's just what's coming underneath.

"That's what you need to actually tackle in the first place. Of course, it means you need to really fully open up the track. That costs a lot of money and time, but honestly, that's the only way to get rid of it because these bumps are not natural and they are out of control."
Verstappen then explained that medical checks had shown that "the bottom end" of his spine "doesn't look that great".

The 29-year-old said: "That I think sometimes people don't really understand that because I can tell you from the checks that I've done from my spine, the bottom end doesn't look that great, the spine.
"I know that's part of racing. I know that can be part of sport, but it's of course also further damage from the cars that we had the last few years.
"Now, if we continue with finding this acceptable to drive on, then, you are going to suffer with that much more."
Norris: I need to take headache tablets
Reigning world champion Lando Norris revealed that he takes headache tablets before driving at certain tracks due to their bumpiness.
Norris also explained that if COTA was a brand-new circuit, it wouldn't meet the requirements to be added to the calendar.
"If you build a new track now, the rules, the regulation of building a new track, the tolerances you have to be within are pretty small," Norris said.
"It certainly doesn't fit anywhere close to what those regulations are now, but it's an old track, not a new track.

"It's pretty bad. There's a lot of places… I need to take headache tablets before I go out simply because it's so bumpy and you're hitting your head pretty hard against the headrests and things because of the bumps. It's certainly not a nice thing.
"There's not much we can do. We complain about it. It's something we've brought up many, many times, but there's only so much we can complain about things."
Mercedes driver George Russell said the bumpy nature of the circuit is "just part of racing," but expressed concern over the general standard of surfaces throughout the year.
"It's bumpy, but I think it's just part of racing," Russell said.

"I'd say my general view is F1 tracks probably need to be repaved every couple of years just to make it a bit more consistent because we're going to tracks now where tarmac's coming up, it's falling apart, it's causing more issues than not.

"We're not an IndyCar or an F2 car that run their ride heights, reasonably high. Our ride heights are 10mm at the end of the straight, a centimetre from the ground, so any time you bump you really feel it.
"The side profile of the tyres now since we've been at the 18-inch is substantially smaller.

"The circumference of the tyre is the same. The circumference of the rim is far greater, so you've lost all of that effective suspension in the tyre, which was a damper, which we kind of don't have anymore. Not ideal, but not much we can do."
