articles.headline: A New Bird-Recognizing Feeder Under $100 Launches for Beginner Bird-Watchers
keyFacts: Birdbuddy released the Birdbuddy Nook smart bird feeder starting at $99 with free AI species recognition.
The device features a 2K-resolution camera, a 3.8-cup seed container, and smartphone alerts via an app.
Birdbuddy ornithologist Mary Mack Gray recommends placing the feeder near shrubs and five to six feet high on a pole.
body: Birdbuddy released its latest line of smart bird feeders equipped with cameras that can detect birds by species on Thursday, and it’s never been a better time to start birdwatching at your home. The reason is a new model called the Birdbuddy Nook, which starts at $99 and offers its AI features for free with no subscription needed.
Read more: The Best Smart Bird Feeders, Tested and Reviewed

Most of the smart bird feeders we’ve tested, including past Birdbuddy models, cost around $200 or more. The particularly affordable Nook includes a 2K-resolution camera with both portrait and landscape orientations, plus a 3.8-cup birdseed container. It wakes up via motion but can keep recording for longer periods of time when there’s lots of activity. All the alerts and species recognition features happen on your phone, via the Birdbuddy app.
More from CNET

The Nook comes in both a standard model for $99 and a model with a solar panel built into the roof for $159. I’ve tested many solar-powered security cameras, and these small panels really do help keep wireless batteries charged for long periods. Since the Nook’s battery is only rated for around a month, and the bird-feeder battery looks a bit more complicated to charge up, I highly recommend the solar model.
Along with the Nook, the company is releasing a Birdbuddy Home mode for $219, which is similar, except it has a larger 6-cup capacity and a wraparound bar for more perching space.
Where should you put the Nook?

Feeders should be placed within 4 feet to 10 feet of shrubs or trees, which is close enough for birds to feel safe from predators, while still being far enough to deter squirrels, according to Mary Mack Gray, Birdbuddy’s in-house ornithologist, who told CNET the best placement options. “If using a pole, a height of 5 to 6 feet off the ground is ideal. Nook is designed for compact spaces like patios, balconies and small yards.”

If you’re worried about squirrels messing up your view or getting in the way, Gray suggests using safflower seeds and suet, which squirrels tend to ignore, and avoid feed like corn or peanuts that squirrels love.
How does the bird recognition feature work?

Birdbuddy uses AI that has been trained on bird species visits to feeders, so it can analyze shape, color, markings and other aspects to pull up a match if one is available. The camera needs a couple of moments to wake up and take a snapshot, as well as a Wi-Fi connection, so you don’t want to put the feeder out too far from your router.

Once a bird lands on the feeder, the feeder will send a snapshot to algorithms for analysis and return an identified species or label it as currently unknown. Birdbuddy doesn’t say if it’s all local AI or if processing is done in the cloud.

CNET’s previous birdwatching reviewer noted that, aside from an occasional misstep, the bird recognition was quite good and even self-corrected itself. That sounds like a handy package for someone who wants to get to know birds in the area while paying the minimum amount.

articles.headline: 8 Cyberpunk 2077 Replay Ideas to Make Night City Feel Brand New
keyFacts: Polygon published a guide detailing eight self-guided replay strategies to make Cyberpunk 2077 feel fresh for returning players.
The article outlines various roleplaying ideas, such as playing as a dual-revolver Nomad, clearing Watson before the main heist, or doing a no-cyberware run.
Other suggested playstyles include using only quickhacks as a netrunner, relying solely on Gorilla Arms for brawling, or turning off the minimap to navigate via landmarks.
body: V is running out of time. That’s the premise of Cyberpunk 2077: a stolen chip is slowly rewriting their mind. The only way out of this particular predicament ushers V through a cast of fixers, rock stars, and corporate killers who all want something from you. And yet, despite those bewildering stakes, there’s a decent chance you spent most of your time in the game clearing gigs, scanning NCPD crime scenes, and wandering Night City’s neon alleys. Then the credits rolled and, within moments, you were back at the character creator.

You’re in good company: Cyberpunk 2077 draws you into that second (or third, or fourth) replay, no matter how many hours you already have in the game. While there’s new content to peruse, such as the brand-new Edgerunners 2 Update, which adds a perk that lets V dual-wield, there are plenty more self-guided replay strats that make this familiar game feel fresh. Here are eight rules to make Night City feel like a place you’ve never been.
8 Be a dual-revolver cowboy
Gig terms: Start as a Nomad, build around revolvers, and look the part.

Nomads are Night City’s outsiders — clans of drifters who live in the Badlands, beyond city limits. If you choose to be among them by selecting a Nomad origin for V, you’ll join the Aldecaldos, the clan that includes Panam Palmer, a hotheaded driver who can become your closest ally. That’s a fabulous setup for roleplaying as an old-fashioned cowboy who’s all about family. Lean into this by donning torn jeans and a hat, ride your bike everywhere, and build V around handguns (especially revolvers). Do so, and you can take advantage of a new trick: The Edgerunners 2 Update’s Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree lets V dual-wield pistols and revolvers from the Power category. If you’re on an older build, a single iron will still do. Just keep the roleplay consistent: Never leave the bike at home, treat every NPC like a neighbor, and let the revolvers do the talking.
7 Clear Watson before the heist
Gig terms: Don’t go to Konpeki Plaza until you’ve finished everything in Watson. Everything.

How long can you put off the biggest job of your life? In Cyberpunk 2077’s opening act, V and their partner Jackie take a job from the fixer Dex. It’s a heist at Konpeki Plaza that sets the rest of the game’s narrative in motion — but there’s nothing actually forcing you to start it. Some players won’t touch it until Watson is cleared, which involves tackling a stretch of gigs, cyberpsycho hunts, NCPD scanner hustles, and side jobs that can put you around level 20 before the heist.

One approach is to treat it as a shopping spree: Level up enough to get Mantis Blades or Gorilla Arms and double-jump legs, then talk to Jackie about Dex’s gig, so V walks into Konpeki Plaza with a signature loadout. Another is to play it as a character beat: This V is too savvy to take the biggest job of their life without a few favors in the bank, so they invest in gigs and scanner hustles as insurance, first. Or you could spend time chasing Street Cred, the reputation meter that unlocks better vendor gear and later gigs. Regardless, by the time you head into Konpeki Plaza, you’ll be overleveled, overequipped, and extremely prepared for the job that changes everything.
6 Do…less
Gig terms: Pick one lifepath, a couple of characters, and one fixer. Ignore everything else.

Completionism is fun, but taking a different tack on a replay can let you focus more deeply on a specific storyline or build. For example, you might decide to prioritize getting Johnny Silverhand, the rockstar whose digital ghost rides along in V’s head, out of their life. That means pursuing that priority at the expense of anything else (you know, like you probably would if you really had Keanu Reeves stuck in your head). That could mean never meeting Goro, the former Arasaka bodyguard, or Panam, Rogue, or Claire, and sticking to Judy among the supporting cast. Looking for other targeted run ideas? Try being a Valentinos loyalist who never leaves Heywood, a Voodoo Boys netrunner who never leaves Pacifica, or a Mox-only run that never leaves Judy’s side. Everyone you skip will still be waiting at the Afterlife on your next run.
5 Go all-natural (relatively speaking)
Gig terms: No cyberware beyond what the story installs for you. Zero exceptions. Even for armor.

Since Update 2.0, almost every piece of armor in Cyberpunk 2077 comes from cyberware, not clothes. Trying to play the game without it feels as strange as strolling into a gunfight wearing a cardigan — which makes this play style such a weirdly energizing prospect. A no-cyberware run means giving up the game’s better armor and a lot of your mobility. A katana, blocking, and a stealth or sniper build will likely be your best bets. Enjoy more freedom to play around with fashion, too: Since clothing is now mostly cosmetic, wear whatever you like. Just be forewarned: Your first run-in with a cyberpsycho will remind you exactly why everyone else installed the chrome.
4 Be a netrunner who never fires a gun
Gig terms: Hack, don’t shoot. Every kill comes from a quickhack.

Netrunners, or hackers who plug into enemy networks with a cyberdeck, use quickhacks to disable, distract, and kill enemies from a distance. At low levels, these short-range code attacks are quite weak, which can translate to a rough first few hours in the game. Survive that, though, and it becomes one of the most overpowered builds in the game: you can jump into a room and take out a group without firing a bullet. You can even remain unseen by chaining Memory Wipe followed by Cyberware Malfunction, which clears enemies without alerting anyone. You can invest absolutely nothing in stealth and the build still does it for you. Just remember: Your cyberdeck is your weapon now, so spend on anything that boosts your RAM.
3 Brawl with Gorilla Arms
Gig terms: Fists only, no hacking, and no other weapons.

Punch first! And then keep punching. The Gorilla Arms are the chrome for players who’d rather settle things up close. Here, a brawler run means no hacking and no weapons. Only the arms. Put your attribute points into Body, which powers the Blunt Weapon perks that directly buff Gorilla Arms, and add Reinforced Tendons, the double-jump legs, to close the distance. Now, with the Edgerunners 2 Update, you have even more options. Five Glamdocs around Night City can now restyle your Gorilla Arms, along with Mantis Blades, Monowire, and the Projectile Launch System. If you’re going to knock an enemy across a room with your bare hands, you might as well do it in hot pink.
2 Turn off the minimap
Gig terms: No minimap. Navigate solely by landmarks and (if you really need it) the map screen.

The absolute fastest way to rediscover Night City is to stop watching the corner of your screen. Turn the minimap off, and, while it may take longer for you to reach your ideal destination, you’ll almost certainly discover places you’ve never seen before. Night City is a vertical city of districts like Kabuki, Japantown, and Pacifica, each with its own landmarks and shortcuts, and you’ll learn them by heart. Use the skyline as your compass: Arasaka Tower looms over everything, just find it to get your bearings. If you want to go further, slow down. With this playstyle, aim for a 100-hour playthrough instead of a 30-hour one. Read every shard. Drive around slowly with the radio on. Play Cyberpunk 2077 like a neon neo-noir novel. It works surprisingly well.
1 Be a sellout
Gig terms: Play a Corpo, pick the self-interested option in every conversation, and side with whomever is winning.

Sometimes it is everyone for themselves, and that’s okay. Cyberpunk 2077 gives you three origins to choose from — Nomad, Street Kid, and Corpo. You can play each as you’d like, but some play styles seem to pair more nicely with some backstories than others. Think: A people’s hero Street Kid, a loyal Nomad who never leaves family behind, or a sleazy Corpo who sided with the cops whenever it seemed profitable to do so. Your origin unlocks its own dialogue options and consequences, so, for example, a Corpo sees doors a Street Kid never will. If being mean to pixels makes you feel bad in real life, this run is good practice. In Night City, everyone has a price. In this run, you’re finally naming yours.

articles.headline: O'Neill bemoans marginal moments but are Celtic just not good enough?
keyFacts: Celtic suffered a 2-1 defeat to Celta Vigo, leaving them with three losses from three Europa League games and 35th in the standings.
Manager Martin O'Neill blamed refereeing decisions and missed chances, while former players James McFadden and Pat Bonner stated Celtic are not good enough at the European level.
Celtic will try to reverse their European form when they host Besiktas in their next match on 5 November.
body: - Published
Three Europa League games. Three defeats for Celtic. They are 35th of 36 teams in the competition after another European collapse, this time against Celta Vigo.
Only Ararat-Armenia and their inferior goal difference keeps the Scottish champions from propping up the table.

Off the back of Sunday's 7-1 drubbing of Hearts, there was hope Martin O'Neill's team had turned a corner. Instead, the disparity between their domestic dominance and European shortcomings was laid bare once more.
After Mika Baur swept Celtic in front on 47 minutes, they went into their shells and succumbed to a timid 2-1 defeat as Javi Rodriguez struck twice in three minutes.
O'Neill bemoaned refereeing decisions and marginal moments that went against his team, but are Celtic simply "not good enough" to compete in Europe?
That was the verdict of former Scotland attacker James McFadden after a Celtic collapse that is becoming all too familiar.
"The performances at this level haven't been good enough," he said on Sportsound. "Celtic are way short."

Celtic looked nailed on for the Champions League this season when they went into a 4-0 aggregate lead against Austrian champions LASK in the play-off round, before shipping five goals in 77 minutes to drop into the Europa League.
O'Neill's side have now lost their last four European matches, conceding 14 goals in the process. Only once before had they done so in the same season - in the 2017-18 Champions League.
"It seems as though Celtic struggle when there's a bit of adversity," McFadden added. "If something goes against them, the confidence drops, their heads drop, they stop playing forward.
"The ball goes back and across, inviting pressure, and there's no way they take the pressure off. That has been a theme."
'Deserved' loss or night of nearly moments?

After another disappointing night, O'Neill focused on moments that went against his team - a free-kick not given before Celta's equaliser and a Liam Scales header that flicked the top of the bar at 1-0.

"We conceded a free-kick and I thought a second before that we should have had a foul for us," O'Neill said. "They score from the free-kick and it knocks us a little bit. It gave them a bit of momentum.

"I think if [Liam] Scales' header goes in to make it 2-0, we get the three points. We've lost three matches now, remarkably we're still in with a chance [of progressing]. We've got to win here and got to win away from home.
"We take the lead in the game, if we get the second goal we win the match and it changes the whole dynamic. It didn't happen, that's it - we need to try to find a way to win European games."
Centre-back Liam Scales had by far the most touches of any Celtic player with 121, well ahead of left-back Kieran Tierney (79) and goalkeeper Sam Johnstone (69).
Goalscorer Baur admitted they did not do enough to win and was at a loss when asked what needs to change. "How we played second half, last 30 minutes, we deserved it in the end," Baur said.
When asked if he knew why his team collapsed in such a manner, he responded: "I cannot tell you, sorry.
"It can happen that you get a goal, they can score too, good team - you should then get control back, hold the ball a bit longer to take the momentum away from them. You should break that."
Celtic did not get control back, did not break Celta's momentum and ultimately paid the price.
"I don't think Celtic are good enough, individually and collectively, to take on a team that's eighth in La Liga," former Celtic goalkeeper Pat Bonner said on Sportsound.
"They moved the ball really well and Celtic couldn't get close to them.
"They are not good enough at this level. Celtic are paying big money for some players because the fans are demanding it and then they come in and aren't good enough."
Their next European outing comes on 5 November as they host Besiktas, trying to reverse their continental woes. Whether they can or not is another matter.

articles.headline: My GOTY is $7 and has 253 Steam reviews
keyFacts: The PC Gamer author stated that the $7 indie game Stuntboost is their favorite game of 2026 so far.
Stuntboost is a fast-paced first-person movement game featuring toy-themed obstacle courses, skateboarding, and precision camera control.
The game includes over 40 levels, layered leaderboards, ghost replays, and hidden collectibles.
body: Fast-paced. 3D Platformer. Parkour. First-Person. Racing.

Those are the tags affixed to the Steam page for Stuntboost, a game that I've had trouble summing up with a clean label when asked about it. Stuntboost is a skateboarding game that sometimes features a car, a platformer with a speedometer, an ode to those shrunken bedroom maps popularized by early FPS modders.
It's also, quite easily, my favorite game of 2026 so far.

Yet, Stuntboost could've easily slipped under my radar. It's been out for a month and hasn't made a big splash on Steam—it's rated "Very Positive" with 253 reviews. I only found it through a friend's recommendation, and even then, the art style didn't immediately suggest it was my thing.

Stunboost's toy fingerboards and cardboard circuits give the impression of a chill, Hot Wheels-adjacent racer your child could enjoy, but unless that child is accomplished with a mouse and keyboard, that ain't happening. This is the only skateboarding game with a warning that suggests you play with a mouse, and it's immediately obvious why.
Once you learn a few techniques, Stuntboost looks like this:
And this.
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
And this.

Despite its choice of vehicles, this thing's for FPS movement sickos—an exercise in precision camera control and first-person platforming. It's essentially a three button game (jump, crouch, grind) about gaining and maintaining speed. Many of its tracks are non-linear obstacle courses that ask you to find your own way across, and the devs actively encourage looking for shortcuts.

I've been obsessed (a word I'm not using lightly) with Stuntboost's 40+ levels for weeks now, replaying tracks and cutting seconds off my times to score the top medals. And once I have those medals, I get to work shaving hundredths of seconds to take the number one spot on my friend leaderboard. Oh man, this is a dangerous game for a friendly rivalry. I now live in fear of a Discord DM informing me that the PB I spent hours honing has been shattered.

But I honestly welcome the excuse to replay tracks, because Stuntboost's movement is fundamentally thrilling, and its maps are masterfully crafted with standard and absurd routing in mind. Its wide ramps, massive jumps, and daring speeds remind me a lot of Trackmania—my favorite racing series—but more specifically, a subset of "full speed" community tracks that never ask you to brake.

Stuntboost also nails a lot of little quality-of-life features that you rarely see in games with way larger budgets. Information about a track is revealed in stages: I can't see friends' times until I've beaten the track once, and global leaderboards are locked until I get the diamond medal. The ghost of my best time appears automatically, but I can also turn on the ghosts of my friends or anyone else on the leaderboard. I can even watch anyone's replay in full as long as I've discovered the same shortcuts they used—a smart touch (possibly inspired by Neon White) that prevents spoilers and entices me to search for what I've missed.
"It's like Neon White"
- Layered leaderboards
- Shortcuts
- First-person platforming

BUT: I never finished Neon White because the levels got overwhelming. Juggling cards and shooting mandatory targets sometimes made levels feel strict and suffocating. Stuntboost is simpler, faster, and improvisational.

Watching replays is a big deal, too, because it's primarily how I picked up on community techniques that opened my third eye: varial kickflips, grind hopping, speed storage. Every sloped surface is an opportunity for just a bit more speed and every ramp-shaped object—be it a plate, playing card, or three-ring binder—is a springboard that could send me across the map. The variability of a single track can be staggering.

Later worlds (which visit other rooms of the same house) expand beyond the skateboard with car levels that revolve around drifting, free roam scooter levels with S-K-A-T-E collectibles, and a longboard that can't jump. Some of these are just a neat palate cleanser, but the car levels are particularly spectacular for how they force me to relearn how I turn and, eventually, hit sick drifts that're impossible on the skateboard.
"It's like Trackmania"
- Ghosts
- High speed
- Wild tracks

BUT: Trackmania is a proper driving game, and Stuntboost is its own thing. Where Trackmania demands braking and cornering to improve track times, Stuntboost has no brake, lets you turn on a dime whenever, and encourages max speed at all costs. If I made a Trackmania, it'd be just like this.

Every level has a hidden tape that unlocks a free cam (excellent for scouting) and contributes to unlocking a set of bonus levels. I haven't played all of these yet, but I'm told there's a huge tower gauntlet with a fierce leaderboard race. There's also a speedrun mode that times a run of the complete game, board skins, and a daily challenge.

I am in awe of how unique and fun and fully-featured this thing is, and for $7. Frankly, it's an injustice that Stuntboost isn't one of the year's big indie success stories, but that's nothing new. The indie games that click for me always gravitate toward interesting movement mechanics or use of physics, and that rarely intersects with what PC gamers are currently going wild about (deckbuilders, autoshooters, and city builders mostly).

I've played lots of those—what I want are more games that make me feel alive and dangerous. Stuntboost has me vibrating in place, leaning into high-speed turns, and cursing a god I don't believe in. It's an intoxicating rush on a level I have not experienced before, and you should absolutely play it.

articles.headline: Switch 2 security takes a hit as hackers unlock homebrew access
keyFacts: Security researcher Sammy Hajhamid demonstrated a software-only partial jailbreak of the Switch 2, granting userland access to run homebrew and mod games.
The exploit utilizes an original Switch version of SmileBasic 4 along with a macOS or Linux PC running a node.js package.
Hajhamid used OpenAI’s Codex to discover an integer overflow and a buffer overflow, which together granted arbitrary read and write privileges.
body: A security researcher has demonstrated a software-only partial jailbreak of the Switch 2, gaining “userland” access that he says “lets us run homebrew, reverse engineer and mod Switch 2 games, back up save files off the Switch, and access most of the Switch 2’s peripherals through MMIO.”

The hack relies on the original Switch version of SmileBasic 4, the latest in a long-running series of programming environments and interpreters that run on Nintendo hardware. The so-called “tethered” hack also requires access to a macOS or Linux PC on the same network to run a node.js package that helps enable privileged system access.

Researcher Sammy Hajhamid writes that he used OpenAI’s Codex to poke at SmileBasic’s language interpreter, using a custom harness that could send USB commands to the system and view results via HDMI (as well as power cycling via a Bluetooth light switch flipping device). After “substantial effort for ~2 weeks,” that harness discovered a 32-bit integer overflow that occurs when removing items from an array in SmileBasic. That error gives access to an array pointer, which in turn allows read and write access to portions of system memory.

From there, Hajhamid writes that he started poking around for access to the Switch 2’s internal sysmodules, looking for ones that could provide more privileged access to the console’s core functions. Eventually, he found a buffer overflow in the console’s FileSystem services module that exposed a cached data pointer, granting arbitrary read and write privileges. From there, Hajhamid writes that he could execute “privileged filesystem actions” and eventually achieve native code execution through a faked filesystem process.

Hajhamid, who goes by Pepsipu online, showed off a host of new modded characters in Mario Kart World as a proof of concept for the exploit. Others are similarly showing off simple demos and in-progress developer tools running on exploited hardware.

articles.headline: Tiger Woods drops major return hint as TGL decision made
keyFacts: Kevin Kisner said Tiger Woods wants to play a full schedule on his Jupiter Links team for the upcoming TGL season.
Kisner stated on a podcast that he was dropped from the team roster because Woods wanted to play.
Season three of TGL begins on December 27, and Woods may also target the Hero World Challenge in December.
body: Whisper it quietly, but Tiger Woods may be closing in on his return to golf.
Woods has been absent from the sport following a rollover crash in March which resulted in a five-year driving ban.
Woods’ last competitive tournament came at the 2024 Open Championship Getty
But a curious roster move on Woods’ TGL team has set tongues wagging about a potential comeback date.
Former US Ryder Cup vice captain Kevin Kisner had been on Woods’ Jupiter Links team for two seasons but was a notable omission when the five-man rosters for season three were released.
When he explained the surprise move, Kisner appeared to let slip Woods’ return to action was not so far away.
Did Kevin Kisner give away Tiger Woods’ comeback plans?
“Well, obviously, I’m not on the team anymore,” Kisner said on Barstool’s Fore Play podcast.
“I had a two-year contract with Jupiter Links and then they, Tiger wants to play. And then they wanted to sign Keith Mitchell, which is totally fine with me.

“And I’m sure I’ll still be involved in some sort of fashion at some point. Go down there and do some stuff for them. You know, the Bad News Bears are still going to be a part of my life, and hopefully they continue to win.”
Kisner was informed of the news via a lengthy text message from Woods’ manager Rob McNamara.
“Rob, Tiger’s guy, he text me a long text last week, I think,” Kisner added.
“Just telling me what they did on their decisions, how they were moving around and what players were going to do and that Tiger wanted to play a full schedule.”
Along with Woods and new signing Mitchell, the Jupiter Links roster includes Max Homa, Tom Kim and Akshay Bhatia.
Woods co-founded TGL alongside Rory McIlroy Getty
Season three of TGL begins on December 27.
Which other competitions could Tiger Woods feature in?
Another competition Woods may target to feature in before the year’s end is the Hero World Challenge in December.
Woods hosts the event each year, which brings 20 of the world’s best golfers to the Bahamas.
The field for this year’s tournament has been released and features the likes of Scottie Scheffler, Cameron Young and Matt Fitzpatrick.
Curiously, there were three blank spaces on the tee sheet for ‘TBA tournament exemptions’, sparking speculation of Woods’ inclusion.
News of Woods’ mooted comeback follows the 50-year-old hitting balls on the range in September, with his swing looking strong.
He has also kept busy by hosting several golf clinics and making public appearances, including a Q&A session at Pebble Beach.

articles.headline: A Line Held Tight is a charcoal visual novel about a miner's strike in the 32nd century and choosing your relationships wisely
keyFacts: Humble Grove is developing A Line Held Tight, a mecha visual novel about a 32nd-century sci-fi miner's strike.
Players control The Canary and make choices that affect relationships with friends, family, and other workers during the strike.
The game features hand-drawn charcoal art and a traditional folk soundtrack, and currently does not have a release date.
body: We've had about roughly four decades of games as we generally know them now, and yet somehow, so often their stories feel so limited in scope. I'm not talking about a lack of big, bold ideas, in fact there might be too many of those. I more mean that there are aspects to life that often go uncovered in games. For example, when was the last time you saw a game about a workers strike? Citizen Sleeper 2 has one questline about such a thing, but it's just what the entire game is about. A Line Held Tight, a mecha visual novel about a sci-fi miner's strike, may bridge that gap.

A Line Held Tight is being developed by Humble Grove, the studio behind the quiet but impactful No Longer Home. Narrative is at the forefront with this game too, albeit with an emphasis on the choices you make throughout the strike. You play as The Canary, a member of a mining colony who's been cut off by the rest of humanity, set in the 32nd century. "As a strike boils over you’ll help The Canary to decide where their heart and their loyalties lie," the game's Steam page explains. "A branching narrative weaves its way through the deep tunnels of the mine to meet the characters within it as outside influences make themselves felt."

Those aforementioned choices you make primarily affect The Canary's relationships with friends, family and other workers, a much more appealing concept mechanically than simply different endings or storylines. In the world of labour organising, it's the relationships you build with others that's really the key thing, so it's nice to see an emphasis on that both narratively and mechanically. The game has some pretty stunning hand-drawn charcoal art too, as well as a traditional folk soundtrack, a pretty unique combo for a game.

As it stands, A Line Held Tight doesn't currently have a release date. Where it makes up for that is a demo that you can try out right now as part of Steam Next Fest, at the very least. There's a nice little video talking through some of the thought process of making a game such as this one from Humble Grove that you can check out below too. And while you're doing that, whether you check out the demo or not, perhaps give the game a little wishlist on Steam.

articles.headline: Would a Democratic Congress change course on Israel?
keyFacts: Voters rarely rank Israel policy among their top priorities, with less than a third prioritizing cutting off aid to Israel according to a poll.
AIPAC announced it would no longer endorse political candidates or make direct campaign contributions.
A Democratic majority in Congress would gain new congressional tools like hearings and funding restrictions, according to analyst Hady Amr.
body: Pro-Palestinian Jewish American demonstrators rally outside AIPAC’s the Manhattan headquarters in February 2024. | Selcuk Acar/Anadolu via Getty Images
This story appeared in Today, Explained, a daily newsletter that helps you understand the most compelling news and stories of the day. Subscribe here .
Israel felt inescapable in the midterm primaries, especially for Democrats, where centrists and progressives clashed — memorably! — over military aid, Gaza, and (of course) AIPAC.

But with the Election Day almost upon us, the subject seems less prominent. When I Googled “Israel US elections” this morning, all the top results concerned next week’s Israeli parliamentary elections.

In less than two weeks, however, Americans will also head to the polls. They’ll decide which party controls Congress, along with a slew of state and local offices. The stakes are arguably unusually high: Voters will choose whether to check the power of a president who has bulldozed over historical norms and limits.

As we count down to that momentous and potentially messy day, I’m partnering with my colleague Astead Herndon and Vox’s The Midterms, Actually team for weekly editions on the biggest issues shaping the midterms. We’re breaking down one issue each week and suggesting further reading and races to watch in November.

Previously, we dug into how both parties are changing , the bipartisan backlash to AI and data centers , and the politics of high costs . This week, we’re tackling Americans’ growing disillusionment with Israel — and how that will (or won’t) show up at the midterm ballot box.
Go a little deeper
View Link
You know the first part of this story already, because we’ve discussed it quite a lot : Americans’ views of Israel have nosedived over the past 18 months.

That shift helped shape the Democratic primaries and will likely figure prominently in the coming presidential contest. But how much Israel matters in a general midterm election, to people outside the political left…well, November will really test that.

Voters rarely rank Israel policy among their top priorities. In a poll that the Associated Press and NORC Center for Public Affairs Research conducted earlier this month, about 80 percent of registered voters said Congress should highly prioritize the cost of living during its next term, and roughly 70 percent said the same about ending the Iran war. By comparison, less than a third of voters said they prioritized cutting off aid to Israel.

There’s another way that Israel factors into US elections, of course — and that’s in fundraising. The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) has become one of the biggest spenders in US elections and a repeat flash point in this year’s Democratic primaries.

But in the general election, even AIPAC has been overshadowed by the GOP’s big-business donors , many of them in tech, who have given Republicans a historic spending advantage in this year’s contests. On Wednesday, the lobbying group actually announced it would no longer endorse political candidates or make direct campaign contributions.

In either case, whatever happens in the midterms won’t likely transform US policy toward Israel. President Donald Trump is still in charge of foreign policy, after all, and even if Democrats take back the House, they’ll have little ability to reverse his agenda.

But a Democratic majority would gain “new congressional tools to act on Israel-Palestine issues,” Hady Amr, the former US Special Representative for Palestinian Affairs, wrote in a new analysis for Chatham House. Those tools aren’t flashy (think: hearings, funding restrictions, and reporting requirements), but they could certainly set the stage for a broader policy shift under a Democratic president.
Races to watch:
Florida’s Senate race , where Democrat Angie Nixon has criticized her party’s ties to the pro-Israel lobby;
Michigan’s Senate race, where Democrat Abdul El-Sayed’s campaign grew out of pro-Palestinian activism ;
Michigan’s (deeply purple) Seventh District , where progressive William Lawrence has vocally criticized US support for Israel.

articles.headline: A new subscription service promises an evolving collection of 'bold and bizarre' indie games
keyFacts: Publisher Pantaloon launched a new $5-per-month subscription service called the Playbill featuring experimental indie games.
Founder Jamin Smith said the service will not feature any games that use generative AI in any form.
The initial lineup includes 13 third-party and first-party titles, with games cycling out when key supplies run out.
body: A new subscription service promises an evolving collection of 'bold and bizarre' indie games
Publisher Pantaloon says the Playbill won't feature games that use generative AI in any way.

Curator-turned-publisher Pantaloon has unleashed a subscription service that fans of indie games might be interested in digging into. The Playbill is a take on Xbox Game Pass, albeit one that focuses on "bold and bizarre" titles.

The initial lineup features third-party games such as Buckshot Roulette, Silt, Ex Sanguis and Cabin Factory. Those sit alongside Pantaloon's own games: Sub-Verge, Occlude, It Takes a War, Boxroom, Rolla and the delightful music creation sim Offbeat.

Much like Game Pass offers first-party Xbox titles (save for new Call of Duty offerings) to subscribers on day one, the Playbill will gain all of Pantaloon's own games as soon as they're released. The service even has its own timed exclusive in the shape of Virtue: Prologue, a visual novella companion piece for Virtue and a Sledgehammer, which is out next week (and a game I'm very much looking forward to.

In addition, the Playbill offers demos, playtests and "abandoned prototypes" for you to check out in a section called the Green Room. At the outset, there are playtests for a few interesting-looking games, namely Isle Goblin, Mr Magpie's Harmless Card Game and Lemonade Apocalypse.

"We want the Playbill to be a celebration of more experimental and eccentric games," Pantaloon founder Jamin Smith said. "The nature of the model reduces that barrier to entry for players to check out genres and experiences that might not be surfaced by Steam's market-shaping algorithms. It's also worth stating that we won't feature or platform any games that use genAI in any form; the Playbill is a celebration of the craft of making games."

Pantaloon moved into publishing after building an audience of more than 50,000 newsletter subscribers, who were able to complete puzzles to receive game keys or pay for codes for its curated titles. The puzzles are free to access on the Playbill, along with the service's community features, Virtue: Prologue and a couple of ARGs. The full lineup of games is available through a Primo subscription, which costs a reasonable $5 per month or $60 per year.

It's worth noting that the service is key-based. Pantaloon will cycle games out of the Playbill when it runs out of keys and it will add new titles on a regular basis. Annual subscribers can snag all 13 games in the initial lineup, as well as each new title that's introduced.

Things are different for monthly subscribers. They'll get a guaranteed game each month, and they won't be able to pick which one. "The monthly titles are part of bespoke partnerships, so the games are defined," Smith told Engadget. "That said, some of our puzzles — like this month's — allow a choice of reward to those that can solve."

If you sign up for a monthly plan, you'll be able to access all of the games after you've been a subscriber for six consecutive months. This is "a mechanism just to prevent somebody getting all 14 titles straight away and then canceling," Smith added.

articles.headline: Sony Continues Its March Towards An All-Digital Future As It Reportedly Kills Off Its Last 4K UHD Player
keyFacts: Sony Japan has discontinued its last remaining 4K UHD Blu-ray player, the UBP-X700/K, according to reports and the company website.
The change reflects Sony's broader trend of reducing investments in physical media and hardware production, such as selling TV factories to TCL.
Physical media fans are concerned that Sony's move signals a broader transition toward an all-digital future.
body: It seems that Sony is exiting the UHD Blu-ray market, as it reportedly has quietly discontinued its one remaining 4K UHD player. It’s part of a larger change at Sony that has seen the electronics and entertainment giant investing less and less in hardware and physical media over the last year or so. And it has fans of physical media nervous.
As first spotted by FlatpanelsHD, the Japanese blog and electronics reseller Kunkoku claimed that sales for the UBP-X700/K are officially ending on October 22 in Japan.

This was the last remaining UHD player manufactured and sold by Sony in Japan. This means that, at least locally, the only new UHD player from the company that will be available is the PlayStation 5. The last major electronics company still making UHD players is now Panasonic. Sony is also, for now at least, still making one DVD player model and one Blu-ray player model.
'Sony reportedly exits UHD Blu-ray player market' https://t.co/WSUgXtk6RJ
'Sony Japan has discontinued its last remaining UHD Blu-ray player, UBP-X700/K, seemingly marking the company's exit.
The news comes via Japanese blog Kunkoku, which happens to also be a Sony retailer.â¦ pic.twitter.com/ZEb1zWA1IK
— Wario64 (@Wario64) October 22, 2026

On Sony Japan’s website, the company lists the UBP-X700/K UHD 4K player as being “Out of stock,” with the added message that “This item will not be restocked,” seemingly confirming Kunkoku’s report. We don’t yet know if Sony intends to globally stop production on the X700/K player, but historically, what happens in Japan tends to be a preview of the company’s larger plans for the rest of the world. So it seems very likely that soon, Sony will be completely done making dedicated UHD players for consumers.

This seems to be connected to Sony divesting from electronics production. Earlier this year, Sony sold off much of its TV and hardware production factories and facilities to TCL as part of a larger deal that also saw TCL take a controlling stake in Sony’s Bravia TV business. Also earlier this year, Sony announced its plan to end PlayStation disc production in 2028.

All of this points to a harsh reality for fans who like to own physical copies of movies and games: That future is likely on the way out as companies look to move toward an all-digital future. Hold on to your discs, folks. Things are going to get rough out there.

articles.headline: PHP2Shell exploit bypasses protections designed to stop remote code execution
keyFacts: VulnCheck researchers developed an exploit that bypasses Address Space Layout Randomization to achieve remote code execution via the PHP2Shell vulnerability.
The PHP Foundation disclosed and issued patches for the critical bugs, identified as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, on Wednesday.
VulnCheck warned that organizations should prioritize patching rather than relying on existing memory protections or configuration changes to stop attacks.
body: Researchers have developed a new exploit that shows how even Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) on an x86-64 server cannot stop the PHP2Shell vulnerability. VulnCheck, which made it available to only the company’s Initial Access Intelligence customers, also warned that threat actors are using AI to find even more ways to attack.

The team told us that it’s a “significant advance” because up until now, ASLR has been a major barrier to exploiting PHP2Shell on real-world servers. They don't expect that to hold, though. “Adversaries are clearly spending time (and tokens) on this bug,” Spencer McIntyre, director of exploit development at VulnCheck, told The Register .
The PHP2Shell mess grew even bigger on Thursday amid reports of attackers abusing the security flaws days before they were disclosed and UK government websites proactively going dark.

Vulncheck's exploit targets CVE-2026-109618 , a critical, out-of-memory corruption bug that leads to remote code execution (RCE) in PHP, and part of the PHP2Shell pair alongside CVE-2026-109619 . The PHP Foundation officially disclosed and issued patches for both on Wednesday.

Overnight, VulnCheck researchers developed what they believe is the first known exploit to achieve remote code execution on ASLR-enabled x86-64 systems with PHP's recommended production configuration.

ASLR is a built-in defense against memory-corruption bugs – like PHP2Shell – that randomly arranges memory locations of a program's key data areas. By scrambling these components live, in memory every time a program runs, ASLR prevents an attacker trying to achieve RCE from correctly guessing the target memory address – and thus prevents them from executing malicious code.
While VulnCheck has seen “hundreds” of PHP2Shell proof-of-concept repositories on GitHub, “very few contain legitimate, working exploits,” McIntyre told us, adding that this is largely due to ASLR.

“There's a significant difference between demonstrating a vulnerability and developing an exploit that can overcome the security protections found in real-world environments,” McIntyre said. “One of the biggest obstacles has been ASLR, a protection designed to make memory corruption vulnerabilities much harder to exploit.”

The threat hunters’ new technique, we’re told, bypasses ASLR. It uses a confirmed memory leak chained into RCE on PHP 8.4.26, and they claim it works on x86-64 platforms even with ASLR enabled and PHP’s recommended display_errors=off production configuration.

“We haven't identified another public or commercial exploit that achieves this under the same conditions,” McIntyre said. “Developing this capability was far from trivial, but it demonstrates that a major barrier to exploiting PHP2Shell on production-configured systems can be overcome.”
VulnCheck says it also works on ARM64, but the RCE is not currently functional on ARM-based systems.

This should be a wake-up call to all organizations that, especially now in the era of AI bug hunting and exploit development , “the technical difficulty of exploiting a vulnerability shouldn't be confused with protection against it,” McIntyre said.
“Organizations running vulnerable versions of PHP should prioritize patching rather than assume existing memory protections or configuration changes will stop an attack.” ®

articles.headline: Zuckerberg wins Meta deal to help him foot bill for possible California billionaire tax
keyFacts: Meta agreed to a new stock deal with chief executive Mark Zuckerberg to keep him from leaving California over a proposed state billionaire tax.
The agreement provides Zuckerberg with more Meta shares and quarterly selling rights to offset potential personal losses from a one-time 5% state tax.
Meta stated the eight-year deal is critically important to maintain Zuckerberg's leadership in California during ongoing industry transformations related to artificial intelligence.
body: - Published
Meta has agreed to a new deal with chief executive Mark Zuckerberg to prevent him from leaving California over a proposed state tax on billionaires.

The agreement gives Zuckerberg, whose wealth is estimated to exceed $200bn (Â£149bn), even more shares in Meta to make up for the fraction of his fortune he may lose if the tax wins voter approval in November.
The measure would impose a one-time 5% tax on residents with a net worth of more than $1bn. It would likely see the Facebook co-founder pay around $10bn in additional state taxes.
He secured the deal with a special committee of Meta after "robust" and "at several points, contentious" negotiations, according to a Wednesday financial disclosure.
California is home to most of the US's technology giants and there are around 225 billionaires who reside in the state, according to the Americans for Tax Fairness campaign group.
The wealth of such people, including Zuckerberg, has ballooned in recent years. Meanwhile, his estimated effective tax rate in California was less than 1%, external each year.

Nevertheless, Zuckerberg told Meta's board last month that he was thinking of moving his primary residence out of California, and even selling his property in the state. His main homes in Californa are in Palo Alto and Lake Tahoe.
Such a move "would be public and inevitably noted and commented upon by company employees", Zuckerberg told the board.
It would also "raise questions for management of the company going forward", he claimed.
In response, Meta decided to create more shares of stock in the company in order to give Zuckerberg a way to essentially make up any wealth he may lose through the tax proposal.

Through what's known as a stock split announced by the company on Wednesday, Meta created an entirely new type of stock and gave one new share to each existing shareholder. Zuckerberg is one of the company's largest shareholders and famously controls the company through the design of his holdings.

Through the deal, he will receive more stock, more often, and also be able to sell it on a quarterly basis, according to the company's financial filing. The shares will not change his level control over Meta, but they will allow him to cash in more easily on the company's value.
The deal appears to be effective even if the one-time tax in California does not pass, and will go on for eight years - as long as Zuckerberg remains a resident of California.
'Critically important'

Meta called the deal with Zuckerberg its "Founder Alignment Agreement," saying it was "critically important" to keep him leading the company from California given the "dramatic and unprecedented transformation taking place in the tech industry and global economy related to artificial intelligence."
The company alluded to problems the company experienced during the Covid-19 pandemic, when Zuckerberg began working outside of the office and mostly from his large compound in Kauai, Hawaii.

After a surge in hiring at Meta during the pandemic, a whistleblower scandal that led to renewed focus on child safety, and a refocus within the company to building out the "metaverse," which included renaming the company Meta from Facebook, the company began mass layoffs and restructuring.
Layoffs have continued into this year. The company's headcount is down 15% from a year ago, meaning it has shed at least 10,000 workers.
Today, the company has moved away from the "metaverse," or virtual platforms, and is more focused on artificial intelligence products and related tools.
With Zuckerberg leading the company's efforts to catch up in the AI race, Meta's board said it sees a future of "tremendous market opportunity" for the company.
Major tech companies are set to spend an estimated $1 trillion, external this year alone developing AI and the costly infrastructure around it, like data centres.
Meta said on Wednesday it planned to spend as much as $145bn this year on AI projects. The company has increased the amount it expects to spend on AI each financial quarter so far this year.

It is spending so much on the technology that it posted negative cash flow for the first time since the company went public 14 years ago. Cash flow represents the money a company retains after paying for operations and investments, meaning Meta is now spending more money than it is bringing in.

And the company intends to spend even more in the year ahead. Susan Li, Meta's chief financial officer, said on Wednesday that another benefit of the stock split would be to give the company more ways to finance future spending on AI work.
The degree of the company's spending on AI, without an clear new revenue stream coming from it, appeared to spook investors on Thursday.
Meta's shares fell more than 7%, wiping more than $100bn off of the company's market capitalisation, a key metric used worldwide to measure the value of a publicly-traded company.

articles.headline: Trump pushback, Biden 'disaster' and gender surprise: 5 key moments from Kansas Senate debate
keyFacts: Republican Senator Roger Marshall and Democratic challenger Adam Hamilton debated in Kansas as both parties compete for U.S. Senate control.
Both candidates addressed personal controversies involving unpaid medical bills and handling church camp abuse allegations.
Hamilton called Biden's border policies a disaster, while Marshall noted he does not always agree with President Trump.
body: Sen. Roger Marshall, R-Kan., and Democratic challenger Adam Hamilton sparred over President Donald Trump, immigration, Iran, transgender athletes, artificial intelligence and personal controversies during a contentious Kansas Senate debate Wednesday night.

The hourlong showdown came less than two weeks before Election Day as Marshall seeks a second term and Hamilton, a longtime pastor, tries to become the first Democrat elected to the U.S. Senate from Kansas since 1932.

The race has drawn increased national attention as Republicans and Democrats battle for control of the Senate, with Trump traveling to Kansas earlier this week to campaign for Marshall — a topic touched on during the debate.
Here are five moments that stood out from Wednesday night's debate.
SLEEPER SENATE RACE EMERGES AS UNEXPECTED HEADACHE FOR REPUBLICANS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS
The debate wasted little time getting contentious, opening with questions about controversies that have fueled attacks against both candidates.
Marshall was confronted with a New York Times review that found his former medical practice sued more than 700 patients over unpaid bills.
"Every year we gave away $3 to $4 million of charity, but we also had a business," Marshall responded. "We had 300 employees, we had a mortgage payment, we had electric."
Hamilton, meanwhile, was questioned about his handling of allegations involving a volunteer at his church's summer camp who was accused of sexual abuse.
Hamilton acknowledged that he should have ensured the individual did not return to the camp following an initial investigation.
FROM 'THIRD REICH' TO ‘NOT THAT INFORMED’: SENATE DEBATES DELIVER FIREWORKS BEFORE MIDTERMS
"I should have checked to make sure that he wasn't going back," Hamilton said. "That was a mistake on my part."
Trump became part of the debate after moderators played footage from the president's campaign appearance for Marshall in Kansas earlier in the week.
"And at this election, I'm asking you to pretend, please, that I'm on the ballot. Just pretend," Trump told the crowd.
Marshall was then asked whether Trump's support meant Kansans should expect him to back every part of the president's agenda.
"No," Marshall responded, saying there had been "multiple times" when he objected to Trump.
Pressed to identify a specific disagreement, Marshall pointed to recent immigration enforcement in southwest Kansas and Trump's approach to beef imports .
"Just like with my wife, I can disagree with her. My wife is always right," Marshall joked. "And President Trump is not always right."
Marshall nevertheless urged Trump voters to turn out for him, arguing that electing Hamilton could help Democrats capture the Senate.
The two rivals found themselves in agreement when the moderator asked each candidate how many genders there are.
"There's two. There's a boy and there's a girl," Marshall said. "I delivered 5,000 of them and almost half were boys and half were girls."
"There are two genders, male and female ," Hamilton responded.
TOP TAKEAWAYS FROM JD VANCE TOWN HALL: COSTLY GAS, DC CORRUPTION, IMMIGRATION HOT TAKES AND THE WAR
The candidates then turned to the debate over transgender participation in women's sports .
Hamilton said decisions over athletic eligibility should generally be made locally but was unequivocal about whether biological males should compete against females.
"I have a 12-year-old granddaughter. I don't want biological men or boys competing against her that could harm her," Hamilton said. "It's not a fair, fair fight."
Marshall argued that by high school, "boys need to be in boys sports, girls in girls sports," while accusing national Democrats of pushing "transgender ideology."
Hamilton later accused Marshall of using the issue to "pick on" and "bully" people.
Hamilton called for greater federal oversight of artificial intelligence and compared the emerging technology to the development of nuclear power and nuclear weapons.
"We developed a Nuclear Regulatory Commission. We need to do the same thing with AI," Hamilton said.
But when the moderator pressed him to identify specific federal regulations he would support, Hamilton acknowledged he did not yet have an answer.
"You know what? I'm not sure, to be honest," Hamilton said, arguing that even experts are struggling to understand the technology's potential dangers.

Marshall advocated a "light touch" approach focused on national security, transparency, protecting children and privacy, while slamming a one-size-fits-all global order for artificial intelligence advancement.
Hamilton pushed back sharply.
"This is an existential — potential existential threat to the human race," Hamilton said. "We can't just go with a light touch and hope everybody does their best."
BIDEN CONSPICUOUSLY ABSENT FROM CAMPAIGN TRAIL AS OBAMA, HARRIS STEP UP FOR MIDTERM PUSH
Hamilton sought to put distance between himself and former President Joe Biden when moderators challenged the Democrat over his claim that he would "lead from the middle."

The moderator pointed to Hamilton's past donations to Democrats, including Biden, former Vice President Kamala Harris and Rep. Sharice Davids, D-Kan., before asking him to identify a progressive policy he opposed.
"The Biden policies when it came to the border were a disaster," Hamilton responded. "I believe in strong and secure borders."
"I'm not somebody who favors the Socialist Party," Hamilton added. "I'm somebody who stands in the middle."
Hamilton also reiterated during the debate that he would not support Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer for majority leader if Democrats capture control of the chamber.
